steps.name: D2: a search that answers 500 makes the host not live, and the binary logs the store error
steps.description: Bugfix D2 (rca.md). The not_live formula (deploy/indexer/host/health-timer.sh:218-221) uses only running, healthz, summary_45m and dids_age. search_probe (:96-109) already runs every 2 min, but its result only goes into the log line. /healthz reports only a poisoned mutex (adapter-index-store/src/lib.rs:167-170), and every other store error becomes a 500 with no log event (search_handler.rs:108 and :145, `map_err(|_store_error| IndexUnavailable)`). So a store that cannot serve searches never pages, and ADR-080 §7 promises more than the code does. Fix (user decision): search_probe captures the HTTP status. not_live also counts search_status == 500. 503 (the busy reply during a pass or purge), 429 and 408 do NOT count. A3's 2-of-2 rule absorbs a single blip. The binary also emits a structured search store-error event with no query text; it is for diagnosis and pages nothing. No new alarm. Update the not_live formula in the script header, observability-design.md, monitoring-alerting.md (A3), the README field table, and the architecture copies that list A3's causes. As a doc-only edit, D1 rides here: correct the evolution note at docs/evolution/indexer-deployment-evolution.md:177. ADR-082 says `1` or unset, and any other value (including 0) is refused, which the code does. First write the regression tests and show they fail against current code.

TEST PARADIGM (mandatory): Unit tests for this step MUST be written as property-based tests using proptest strategies + state-delta assertions over a declared universe. Single-example unit tests are FALLBACK only — document why in a `// bypass:` comment if used. Acceptance scenarios are framed as properties where the contract supports it; classic scenarios are fallback. Integration and E2E tests REMAIN single-example — they verify wiring, not invariants.
STAGE CONTEXT: bug-prone legacy code = Stage 1 (state-delta capture of hidden mutations first).
DESIGN: contract shapes. The not_live decision is pure-function over the probe results. The probes are the shell's effects; keep them separate from the formula. search_probe returns the HTTP status alongside search_ok and search_ms. Use curl's %{http_code}, without -f, so a 500 is still read; 000 or no output becomes 0. Define search_ok explicitly from the status: 1 ONLY for a 2xx answer, 0 for everything else (4xx, 5xx, 0). Dropping -f must never leave search_ok undefined or 1 for an error status. not_live adds `search_status == 500` and nothing else. Do NOT count 503, 429 or 408, and do not count 0 (connect failure or timeout), so a busy pass or purge never pages. Add search_status to the printf of the health line (a new numeric field; keep every existing field and its order otherwise). The A3 metric filter keys on $.not_live, so no tofu change is needed. Confirm deploy/tofu/environments/prod/indexer.tf needs nothing. Binary side: mirror the existing TruncationLog seam. search_handler gains a second report hook (for example StoreErrorLog = Arc<dyn Fn(SearchStoreError) + Send + Sync>, carrying the dimension only). Both map_err sites (the dimension query and suggest_object) report through it before returning IndexUnavailable. The composition root (run.rs, next to emit_search_truncated at ~:454/:522) emits {"event":"indexer.search.store_error","dimension":...} as one structured line. Never log the value or the raw store error text (WD-105, I-IXD-4). The handler must stay read-only by type: the new hook name must not trip `xtask check-arch` indexer_search_handler_read_only. The crafter picks the names; the data-models row must match what ships. xtask test seam: extend health_run_with (xtask/tests/indexer_deployment_platform.rs:570) so the curl stub can answer the search with a given status (it must honour -w '%{http_code}' / '%{time_total}' the way the script now calls it). This stub currently always succeeds (:576-579). Update XP-13/XP-14 stubs only as far as the new curl call shape requires. Oracles use literal statuses and literal expected fields ("not_live":1, "search_status":500), never a recomputation of the formula. Docs: script header (:12-19), docs/feature/indexer-deployment/devops/observability-design.md (§4 not_live row ~:61, field table ~:57, sample line ~:48), docs/feature/indexer-deployment/devops/monitoring-alerting.md (A3 description ~:53 and the runbook cause list), deploy/indexer/README.md (field table ~:274: a `search_status = 500` row pointing at indexer.search.store_error), docs/architecture/indexer-deployment/architecture-design.md (~:253 and ~:353 A3 causes), and the event catalogues docs/architecture/indexer-deployment/data-models.md (~:93) and docs/feature/indexer-deployment/design/data-models.md (~:88). Add a dated amendment note to ADR-080 §(7) citing this RCA: a store error is now logged and a search 500 counts toward A3. D1 rides here as a doc-only edit: correct L3 in docs/evolution/indexer-deployment-evolution.md:177 and mark L5 resolved.
LESSONS: oracles must use concrete literal values, never call or mirror the code under test. Run dependent suites narrowly (`cargo test -p cli --test <target>`, `cargo test -p xtask --test <target>`), never the whole workspace on the host (CI verifies the full suite). Build openlore-indexer before acceptance tests so they exercise the current binary. Keep main green: the regression tests and the fix land in the same commit. deploy/** changes are checked in CI by deploy-pds-check, whose shellcheck is stricter than local 0.11.0, so run `shellcheck -S info` on every touched script.

steps.name: D4: the four self-referential oracles become literal and fail against a wrong implementation
steps.description: Bugfix D4 (rca.md), test-only. Four oracles agree with the code under test because they come from it or mirror it, so a wrong implementation can pass them. (1) The TEST_FAULT property (crates/openlore-indexer/src/config.rs:747-766) builds its inputs from TestFault::ALL / token() and its oracle from TestFault::from_token. (2) CORE-4 `list_oracle` (tests/acceptance/indexer_deployment_core.rs:251-265) re-implements the reader, and `sut_read_did_list` (:125-130) drops the refusal's `problem`. (3) CORE-5 `sut_pass_exit` (:132-152) lets the harness choose which failure wins (find_map order), so the property only checks cause.is_some() == (code == 2). (4) The control round-trips (crates/openlore-indexer/src/control.rs:362-391) only check that encode and decode agree with each other. Fix (user decision): fix all four. Every assertion becomes STRONGER, never weaker. Each new oracle uses concrete literal values and is shown to FAIL against at least one deliberately wrong implementation (a temporary local mutation, reverted and recorded in the commit message or step log). No production behaviour changes. If a literal oracle exposes a real defect, stop and report it rather than fixing it inside this step.
criteria: TEST_FAULT: the oracle is a literal table of (token, expected outcome): each known token string written out as a literal loads exactly that fault in a development build; literal unknown or near-miss tokens (wrong case, a trailing space, a prefix of a real token, empty) are refused naming OPENLORE_INDEXER_TEST_FAULT and the value; every value is refused in a release build. No input or expectation is derived from TestFault::ALL, token() or from_token. Shown to fail against a wrong implementation (for example from_token accepting an extra token, or a release build accepting one).
TestFault::ALL coverage: a literal-count check (or an exhaustive match in the test) fails when a fault is added without a literal row, so the table cannot silently fall behind.

CORE-4: sut_read_did_list keeps the refusal's problem (NotADid, NotWellFormed, NamesNoRepo). The scenario asserts against a literal example table modelled on crates/appview-domain/tests/deployment_contracts.rs:70-128 (entry text -> Loaded(literal list) or Malformed(literal entry, literal problem)). Any remaining property checks only properties that do not mirror the reader (for example a list built from known-good literal DIDs with separators and duplicates loads them first-seen and distinct). list_oracle no longer re-implements the reader. Shown to fail against a wrong implementation (for example the wrong problem for did:key, or last-seen order).

CORE-5 (rescoped, no production change): the code under test receives at most ONE failure, and the harness's find_map precedence is removed entirely. A literal table maps each PassFailure to its exact cause token and exit 2, and literal per-DID summaries with no failure to 3 (every listed DID skipped) or 0. Shown to fail against a wrong implementation (a wrong token or a wrong exit code). Which failure wins stays in openlore-indexer ingest_pass.rs (the first failure ends the pass) and is covered by acceptance tests, not by this property.

Control wire: literal assertions pin the exact wire text. encode_request(RunPass) == "{\"request\":\"run_pass\"}\n", encode_request(Probe) == "{\"request\":\"probe\"}\n", and literal reply lines for completed, busy and ready decode to the literal expected ControlReply (and encode to them, modulo key order if serde does not fix it). Shown to fail against a wrong implementation (for example a renamed wire token on both encode and decode, which the round-trip alone cannot catch).
No test is deleted without a stronger replacement. The existing concrete tests in config_contracts.rs and deployment_contracts.rs stay green, and every touched suite passes against current code.

steps.implementation_notes:
TEST PARADIGM (mandatory): Unit tests for this step MUST be written as property-based tests using proptest strategies + state-delta assertions over a declared universe. Single-example unit tests are FALLBACK only — document why in a `// bypass:` comment if used. Acceptance scenarios are framed as properties where the contract supports it; classic scenarios are fallback. Integration and E2E tests REMAIN single-example — they verify wiring, not invariants.
STAGE CONTEXT: bug-prone legacy code = Stage 1 (state-delta capture of hidden mutations first).
DESIGN: the code under test is unchanged; only oracles and SUT bindings change. All four contracts are pure-function, so a literal table is the strongest oracle. Wrap each table in a proptest that walks the table (select over its rows) plus generated near-misses, or mark single-table tests `// bypass: literal oracle table; a generator would have to mirror the code under test`. The rule for every oracle: it may NOT call, import or re-implement the function it checks. Literal inputs and literal expected outputs only. Generators may produce inputs, but the expected value for a generated input must come from a literal (for example near-miss tokens are always refused, and known-good literal DIDs always load). (1) TEST_FAULT: keep the release-build refusal check. Replace TestFault::ALL / token() / from_token in both generator and oracle with a literal ("first_pass_panics", TestFault::FirstPassPanics)-style table copied from the documented tokens (the crafter reads the real list from config.rs:~121 and config_contracts.rs:~164 ONCE, writes it as literals, and does not reference them from the test). Add an exhaustive `match` over TestFault in the test so a new variant forces a new row. (2) CORE-4: change ListReadView::Malformed to carry the problem (a local enum mirroring EntryProblem's variant names) and bind sut_read_did_list to keep bad.problem. Delete list_oracle and well_formed_repo_did as oracles. Use a literal table (at least: the empty text, separators of comma/space/CRLF, duplicates, a BOM-prefixed first entry -> NotADid, did:key -> NamesNoRepo, did:PLC -> NotWellFormed, the 2048/2049-byte boundary, first bad entry wins). (3) CORE-5 (orchestrator decision: RESCOPE, no production change): pass_exit takes Option<PassFailure>, so the SUT gets at most ONE failure. Remove the harness's find_map precedence entirely, and reshape the generated outcome to an optional single failure plus per-DID outcomes. The literal table maps each PassFailure to exit 2 and its exact cause token (read the tokens from data-models §4, not from PassFailure::token()). With no failure, literal summaries give 3 (non-empty, all skipped) or 0. Pass-failure precedence stays in openlore-indexer ingest_pass.rs (the first failure ends the pass) and is covered by acceptance tests, not this property. Update the CORE-5 doc comment and the module table row (:14) to match. (4) control.rs: add the literal wire test next to the round-trips. Compare parsed JSON values (serde_json::Value from a literal) if key order is not guaranteed, and assert the trailing newline literally. Mutation demonstrations: for each of the four, apply one deliberately wrong change locally, run the narrow test, see RED, revert. Record the four mutations and their RED test names in the commit message. Never commit a mutation. This is test-only, so the RED phase of the step is the mutation demonstration, not a failure against current code.
LESSONS: oracles must use concrete literal values, never call or mirror the code under test. Run dependent suites narrowly (`cargo test -p cli --test indexer_deployment_core`, `cargo test -p openlore-indexer <filter>`), never the whole workspace on the host (CI verifies the full suite). Keep main green: every touched suite passes against current code before commit. deploy/** is not touched in this step.

steps.name: D3: render-secrets replaces each secret file by rename and never swaps the directory
steps.description: Hardening D3 (rca.md). compose bind-mounts /pds/app/secrets:/run/secrets:ro. deploy/review-app/host/render-secrets.sh:55-58 renames the directory away and moves a staging directory in, then deletes the old one (:22). A running container keeps the old (deleted) directory inode. If `docker pull` (deploy.sh:235) fails after rendering, the old container keeps running against an empty /run/secrets. Fix (user decision): write each secret to a temp file in the SAME directory, chmod and chown it, then rename it over its final name (as render-dids.sh does). Remove stale files whose parameter no longer exists. Never rename, remove or recreate the directory itself. Rotation stays restart-based. The required-parameter check still runs before anything in the live directory changes. Write the xtask regression test first and show it fails today.
criteria: Two consecutive renders against stub aws (different values the second time) leave the secrets directory with the SAME inode, replace each secret file (new inode, new content), keep every file mode 0400, and leave no staging or temp file and no .secrets.old / .secrets.new.* sibling. FAILS TODAY (the directory inode changes).
A parameter present in the first render and absent from the second is removed from the directory after the second render. Files for parameters still present are not removed.

A render whose required parameter (client-jwk, data-key, github-token, log-salt) is missing or empty exits non-zero, and the FULL directory listing is unchanged: the same set of entry names (dotfiles included) with byte-identical contents. A leftover `.<name>.new` temp file therefore fails the check.
No secret value appears on stdout or stderr in any of these runs (sentinel values).
shellcheck -S info passes on render-secrets.sh, and deploy-pds-check is green in CI.

steps.implementation_notes:
EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: shell artefact; compensate with the xtask integration test.
STAGE CONTEXT: bug-prone legacy code = Stage 1 (state-delta capture of hidden mutations first).
DESIGN: contract shape is bounded-change. The declared mutation set is the regular files directly inside SECRETS_DIR whose names are the rendered parameter names, plus the removal of stale ones. The directory inode, its mode and its owner are outside the set and must not change. Order: (a) fetch every parameter into temp files INSIDE SECRETS_DIR (same filesystem, so rename is atomic). Use a dot-prefixed temp name that cannot collide with a parameter name, for example `.<name>.new`. The parameter-name filter already rejects names that are not [A-Za-z0-9._-], and the crafter must make sure a temp name can never equal a real parameter's name. (b) Check that every REQUIRED name has a non-empty temp file. On failure remove the temp files and exit 1 with the live files untouched. (c) chown and chmod 0400 each temp file. (d) mv -f each temp over its final name. (e) Remove regular files in SECRETS_DIR that are not in the rendered set (stale), never the directory. (f) A trap removes leftover temp files on any exit. Create SECRETS_DIR (0700, owned by APP_UID) only if it does not exist. Never mv or rm -rf it. Keep values off stdout and stderr (set +x stays). Update the header comment (the swap paragraph at :53-54). Check docs/feature/bluesky-claim-review-app/devops/infrastructure-integration.md §5 and deploy/review-app/README.md for a description of the directory swap, and amend it if present. xtask test: add it to xtask/tests/indexer_deployment_platform.rs (it already holds XP-2 for the review-app compose and has the Stubs, bash and inode helpers). Tag it XP-19 in the module doc. Stub `aws` so get-parameters-by-path prints the names and get-parameter prints a per-name sentinel value from a file the test controls between runs. Stub `chown`. Point REVIEW_APP_SECRETS_DIR at a tempdir and REVIEW_APP_SSM_PATH at a literal path. Oracles are literal: literal names, literal sentinel values, literal mode 0o400.
LESSONS: oracles must use concrete literal values, never call or mirror the code under test.
